title: Constants descent and projectivity for a supplied semilinear quotient
statement: Let $e$ be a field [def-weil-field], $K/e$ a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and $H$ a finite group [def-sfb-finite-infinite-set] acting on $K$ by $e$-automorphisms. Put $F=K^H$, the subfield fixed by every element of $H$. Let $Y$ be a smooth projective $K$-scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-kun-projective] with an action of $H$ by $e$-scheme automorphisms such that $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is equivariant. Suppose a scheme $Q$ [def-pc-scheme] and an invariant finite surjective morphism $q:Y\to Q$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism] are given. Assume that for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ the map $Y(\Omega)\to Q(\Omega)$ is onto with fibres precisely the $H$-orbits, that $\mathcal O_Q=(q_*\mathcal O_Y)^H$, and that every invariant morphism $Y\to T$ to a scheme factors uniquely through $q$. Then there is a unique structure morphism $s_F:Q\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ satisfying $s_Fq=(Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}F)$. Its induced $e$-structure is the descent of the given $e$-structure of $Y$, and $q$ is a morphism over both $F$ and $e$. The scheme $Y$ is normal and Noetherian and is a finite disjoint union of open and closed normal integral schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme] [def-weil-irreducible-components]; $Y$ is projective over $F$ and $e$. The scheme $Q$ is normal and Noetherian, projective over $F$ in the finite-projective-space convention, and proper of finite type over both $F$ and $e$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Here normal means that each local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Empty and disconnected schemes and nonfaithful actions are allowed. No quotient-existence assertion is made.

proof.text: Write $a:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $a_F:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ for the given structure map and its composite. The fixed elements form a subfield $e\subseteq F\subseteq K$: sums, products and inverses of fixed elements are fixed. Both $F/e$ and $K/F$ are finite: $F$ is an $e$-linear subspace of the finite-dimensional space $K$, and any finite $e$-spanning set of $K$ also spans it over $F$. Equivariance and fixedness of $F$ give $a_Fh=a_F$ for every $h\in H$. Apply the assumed categorical property to this invariant map to obtain the unique $s_F:Q\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ with $s_Fq=a_F$. Composing with $\operatorname{Spec}F\to\operatorname{Spec}e$ gives $s_e$ and $s_eq=a_e$. Any other such $e$-structure equals $s_e$ by the same categorical uniqueness. Thus $q$ is over $F$ and $e$, with the asserted descended $e$-structure.

source.place: Expose X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.151, constants S1/L in diagram (2.c); elementary use of the supplied categorical universal property.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-constant-projective-graph] with extension $K/F$, source $R=Y$, target $S=\operatorname{Spec}F$, and $c=a_F$. The target is separated over $F$ (its relative diagonal is the identity). Taking $S'=S$ gives projectivity of $Y$ over $F$ in the finite-projective-space convention and properness of $a_F$. Apply the same statement with $K/e$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}e$ to get projectivity and properness over $e$. Properness includes finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. These uses require no separability of the constant extensions.

proof.text: The field $F$ is Noetherian, since its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal, so $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is Noetherian with its single affine chart. Since $a_F$ is of finite type, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $Y$ Noetherian. Independently, smoothness over $K$ gives regularity of $Y$ by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular]. Clause (1) of [rem-pc-regular-normal] gives normality, and clause (2) gives the required finite disjoint union of open and closed normal integral components of $Y$. No connectedness or nonemptiness assumption is used.

source.place: Tag 056S (lemma-smooth-regular), with morphisms.tex Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian) and properties.tex Tags 0569 and 033M (regular-normal and normal Noetherian decomposition).

proof.text: The $H$-action is by $F$-automorphisms of $Y$, because $a_Fh=a_F$, and it is by $e$-automorphisms by hypothesis. The supplied categorical property also holds in $F$-schemes: for an invariant $F$-map $b:Y\to T$ with structure $t:T\to\operatorname{Spec}F$, let $\bar b:Q\to T$ be its unique factor as a scheme map. Then $(t\bar b)q=tb=a_F=s_Fq$, and categorical uniqueness for the map $a_F$ gives $t\bar b=s_F$. Thus the factor is an $F$-map, uniquely. The identical argument with $e$ shows the categorical property over $e$. Now apply [lem-sfb-finite-quotient-normal-proper] over $F$, and again over $e$: the source is normal proper finite type by steps 2--3; the finite surjection, invariant structure sheaf and geometric-orbit hypotheses are exactly those supplied. It follows that $Q$ is normal and Noetherian, and proper of finite type over both $F$ and $e$.

source.place: Expose X 2.3 Step 2, diagram (2.c), p.151; the general supplied-quotient theorem uses Stacks Tags 00IS, 09MQ(4), 03GN, and the normal affine invariant-ring calculation.

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of [rem-pc-regular-normal] to $Q$: write it as a finite disjoint union $Q=\coprod_{i\in I}Q_i$ of open and closed normal integral schemes. Choose a closed projective-space embedding of $Y$ over $F$ from step 2. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ample-invertible] its pullback of $\mathcal O(1)$ is an ample invertible module $M$ on $Y$.

source.place: Tags 033M (lemma-normal-Noetherian), 0357 (lemma-normal-locally-finite-nr-irreducibles), 01PS (definition-ample), and 01PU (lemma-ample-on-closed); the projective-ample node includes the projective-space input.

proof.text: For $i\in I$ let $W_i=q^{-1}(Q_i)$, with its open subscheme structure. This is open and closed in $Y$. Its inclusion $j_i:W_i\to Y$ is a closed immersion: it is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset and $\mathcal O_Y\to(j_i)_*\mathcal O_{W_i}$ is surjective, with identity stalk maps on $W_i$ and zero target stalks off $W_i$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The restricted map $q_i:W_i\to Q_i$ is finite: every affine open $V\subseteq Q_i$ is an affine open in $Q$, and its inverse image and ring map under $q_i$ are those under $q$, so [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] applies. It is surjective because $q$ is surjective. The restriction $j_i^*M$ is ample by [lem-trf-ample-restrict-closed-immersion]. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-normal-ample-descent] to the finite surjection $q_i$, whose target $Q_i$ is normal integral, obtaining an ample invertible module $L_i$ on $Q_i$. No assertion of descent of the particular module $M$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0BD4 (proposition-push-down-ample), case (2), applied separately to normal integral quotient components; properties.tex Tag 01PU for restrictions.

proof.text: Define a sheaf of modules $L$ on $Q$ by $L(U)=\prod_{i\in I}\Gamma(U\cap Q_i,L_i)$, with componentwise restrictions and the action of $\mathcal O_Q(U)$ by restriction. The sheaf axiom holds componentwise. Its restriction to $Q_i$ is $L_i$, so it is locally free of rank one, hence invertible by [def-sc-invertible-module]. It is ample by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]: $Q$ is quasi-compact by step 4, and for $x\in Q_i$ choose $n\geq1$ and a global section $u$ of $L_i^{\otimes n}$ whose nonvanishing locus is affine and contains $x$. Extend $u$ to a section of $L^{\otimes n}$ by zero on the other disjoint open components. Its nonvanishing locus is exactly $(Q_i)_u$, an affine open of $Q$. This proves the required affine-locus condition. If $I$ is empty, the construction gives the unique module on the empty scheme; local rank one and the affine-locus condition are vacuous, and the empty scheme is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 01PS (definition-ample), verified explicitly for a finite disjoint clopen union; elementary componentwise sheaf construction.

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}F$. It is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: its only opens are $S$ and the empty set, both quasi-compact, and intersections of affine opens are among these. The proper map $s_F$ is quasi-compact, and $L$ is $s_F$-relatively ample: its restriction over the whole affine base is ample by step 7, and the empty restriction satisfies the same definition vacuously. Apply [lem-sfb-proper-relative-ample-projective-bundle] to obtain projectivity of $s_F$ in the projective-bundle sense. The trivial invertible module $\mathcal O_S$ is ample: the section $1$ in tensor degree one has affine nonvanishing locus all of $S$, and $S$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Therefore [lem-trf-projective-bundle-to-h-projective] makes $s_F$ projective in precisely the finite-projective-space convention [def-kun-projective]. The normality, Noetherianity, properness and finite-type clauses were already obtained in steps 3--4, and the constants and compatibility clauses in step 1.

tool_uses.why: Smoothness over a field gives regularity, without dimension or connectedness assumptions; the unit supplies no different regularity theorem.

Restriction of an ample module to a closed component is ample, needed before applying 0BD4(2); the unit does not replace this generic restriction theorem.
